findings.text: reclaim-or-refuse crashes rather than refuses on a claim record whose pid is out of range. _claim_holder_is_alive (:1626) calls os.kill(holder_pid, 0) at :1645 without catching OverflowError, so a record carrying a pid larger than C int -- which only a corrupted or foreign writer produces, since the code stores os.getpid() -- propagates OverflowError out of _claim_node_dispatch instead of the D12 refusal. Reproduced against the reviewed head: _claim_holder_is_alive({'pid': 10**30, 'process_start_time': '0'}) raises OverflowError 'Python int too large to convert to C int'. A pid of 999999 with a start time now returns False, so the original wedge is fixed; this is the residual crash path. Fix: catch (OverflowError, OSError) around os.kill and treat an uninterrogable pid as present, the conservative answer already given to a record with no pid or start time. Secondary and unreaped: _reclaim_stale_node_dispatch_claim (:1656) renames a stale claim to '<name>.reclaimed-<run_id>' under the claims directory and nothing removes it, so reclaimed files accumulate; harmless at the rate reclaims occur, but unbounded.
